necessary_context.applies_to: Algorithm and Theorem in this batch
necessary_context.content: R^N is decomposed into n coordinate blocks with positive integer dimensions n_i, N=sum_i n_i, I_N=(U_1,...,U_n), x=sum_i U_i x^(i), and g_i(x)=U_i^T grad f(x). This batch selects Euclidean block norms. The source defines s# as a maximizer of <s,h>-||h||^2/2; in Euclidean geometry s#=s.
necessary_context.name: Block geometry and sharp map

necessary_context.content: f is convex and differentiable on all R^N; X*=argmin f is nonempty and bounded. Known positive finite L_i satisfy ||g_i(x+U_i h)-g_i(x)||_2<=L_i||h||_2 for every block i, x and h. The extracted finite performance bound explicitly requires finite R_{1-alpha}(x0).
necessary_context.name: Standing convex assumptions

necessary_context.content: S_alpha=sum_i L_i^alpha, p_i=L_i^alpha/S_alpha. ||v||_beta^2=sum_i L_i^beta||v^(i)||_2^2; ||g||_{beta,*}^2=sum_i L_i^(-beta)||g^(i)||_2^2. R_beta(x0)=max_{x:f(x)<=f(x0)} max_{x* in X*}||x-x*||_beta. The inner operation is maximum, not distance to the nearest minimizer.
necessary_context.name: Weighted norms, probabilities and maximum radius

necessary_context.content: The sampling counter and RCDM input explicitly allow alpha in R. PDF p.7 introduces S_alpha with alpha>=0, but Lemma 2 on that page explicitly states any real alpha. This extraction uses the displayed finite sum for real alpha with positive L_i; the Theorem record separately supplies a complete reconstruction.
